M1_DENSITY_MATRIX.summary: Canonical recipe produces densities 85x lower than per-task weighted recipe on average. The two recipes occupy fundamentally different density scales, confirming the recipe choice is not a minor parameter but a structural regime change.

M5_DOMINANCE_MEAN.description: Mean dominance across all task-definition-recipe triples. With 2 recipes, dominance is necessarily 0% or 100% (binary), so mean=50% is trivially expected and uninformative.

M6_DOMINANCE_SD.description: Standard deviation of dominance. Trivially 50% given binary 0/100% distribution with 2 recipes.

M7_CLASSIFICATION_ENTROPY.description: Low entropy indicates classification is heavily concentrated on MEDIUM (13/14 pairs). Only detail_camera canonical recipe classified as HIGH. Discrimination is present but narrow.

M8_NULL_CONTROL_DOMINANCE.description: Null control (shuffled recipe labels) produces identical dominance mean. With 2 recipes, shuffling preserves the binary structure, making this control uninformative for detecting recipe effects.

M9_NULL_CONTROL_CI_WIDTH.description: Null CI width is 125x larger than original, indicating recipe assignment has massive effect on ranking stability. This is the most informative control result.

artifacts.note: Source measurement data: 7 tasks, 3 definitions, locatable_sample capped at 20 elements
Complete analysis output: density matrix, dominance pairs, ranking CIs, classification, null controls
Analysis script implementing OECD/COINr-style sensitivity analysis on density data

observations.description: Canonical recipe (p=0.5 independent inclusion) produces near-zero densities: mean 0.006 across all task-definition pairs. Per-task weighted recipe produces task-type-dependent densities: product_listing ~0.56-0.65, detail ~0.30-0.50, cart ~0.29-0.44.

Cross-recipe density ratio is 84.7x. The two recipes do not merely differ in magnitude — they occupy fundamentally different density regimes. Canonical treats the page as nearly empty; weighted treats it as 30-65% full.
Dominance pairs are strictly degenerate: 0% (canonical loses) or 100% (weighted wins) across all 42 task-definition-recipe triples. No task-definition pair shows competitive dominance (10-90%).

Ranking CIs are narrow (width 1-4) with per-task weighted producing width=1 for all tasks. Canonical shows width=2 for product_listing tasks and width=4 for detail_camera. Recipe choice dramatically affects ranking certainty.
Classification: 13/14 task-recipe pairs classified MEDIUM, 1/14 (detail_camera canonical) classified HIGH. Low entropy (0.37 bits) indicates poor discrimination.
Within each recipe, the three definitions produce highly correlated rankings (Spearman r > 0.98). The definition choice is not the primary source of recipe sensitivity — the recipe choice itself is.

validity_notes.note: The OECD/COINr dominance framework is designed for comparing 3+ alternatives. With exactly 2 recipes, dominance is necessarily binary (0% or 100%), making C2_DOMINANCE_INFORMATIVE trivially fail. This is a framework limitation, not a scientific finding.

Canonical recipe uses expected density (average over 1000 random iterations), not a single stochastic realization. This produces stable near-zero values. A single realization would show variance but still concentrate near 0.005-0.01.

Per-task weighted recipe normalizes by elements_with_bbox/1500, introducing an implicit weight that amplifies the recipe's structural difference from canonical. The weight is not a parameter choice but a consequence of how the recipe scales inclusion probability.

Raw evidence contains locatable_sample capped at 20 elements per task. Actual locatable element counts are 21-82. The cap truncates the true density computation, likely underestimating densities for tasks with >20 locatable elements.
Null control with 2 recipes is structurally uninformative for dominance (shuffling preserves binary structure). The CI width null control is informative and shows massive effect (125x ratio).

C3_CI_INFORMATIVE passes because CI widths (0.0185-0.0739) are well below the density range (0.417-0.641). However, this is partly because the density range is inflated by the cross-recipe scale difference.
